summary: No reachable vulnerabilities. Trust boundary 1 (stored IndexedDB hand records): parseHandRecord's checkDecisions bounds the decisions array to 0..400 dense entries (MAX_ACTIONS), requires every entry to be a non-array object, checks enums against fixed allow-lists (STREETS, user action types, POSTFLOP_RULE_IDS, GRADE_LABELS keys, GRADE_RULE_IDS) via includes (no coercion), requires whole/safe-integer amounts and finite 0..100 percentages, caps opponentBasis at 9 entries with seats limited to dealt-in seats, caps text at 200 and explanation at 2000 characters, and requires a boolean hinted. It then cross-checks the count, street, type and amount against the already-validated user non-blind actions. Worst-case work and memory per record are bounded (about 400 x (2 KB + 9 x 200 chars)). Error messages contain only field paths built from fixed names and indices, never stored values. Stored strings reach no HTML sink: there is no innerHTML/insertAdjacentHTML in src, and the decisions are not rendered yet, so later UI work should keep using text nodes. Trust boundary 2 (observed-stats snapshot over the worker boundary): ranges.ts still converts a non-array to [] before observedBySeat. The new loop rejects null, primitive and array entries and seats that are not safe integers 1..10 with RangeError before any Map or number use, and handleAdviceRequest turns all throws into ok:false, which fails closed. This closes TASK-7.13's non-object-snapshot-entry-typeerror. The write path (decisionRecord) builds fresh plain objects and arrays with spread/map, so it shares no references with live state. No new dependencies, secrets, network, crypto or randomness changes.
